content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm having trouble figuring out how to reset output values using an input. In my example, pressing I5 keeps adding 10 through the chain. How can I use an input to reset the values to zero? My submitted program is just a snippet from a larger one, showing what I'm trying to resolve. Any guidance is appreciated.
The setup acts as an analog counter. Adding a button to B094 will reset the counter. Could you clarify what exactly is causing trouble?
Can you please clarify what you're asking?
Could you explain the circuit's intended function, and why you believe the counter isn't resetting to zero? Where specifically do you see the issue?

First off, thanks for your assistance. As a hobbyist, I have a lot to learn. I'm still working on understanding the And(edge) concept over time. See the new section from my program: I2 adds 10 and I1 resets the counter, as you explained before. With NI17, 18, 20, 22, these add to the sequence, while NI21 subtracts 5 and NI19 inhibits analog output without resetting to zero. I tried your recommended solution, linking an input to B104 to reset the sequence, but I'm unsure how to apply this approach to the NI sequence logic. Any suggestions?
This is proving difficult; I've been unable to get NI19 to fully reset the sequence, regardless of my approach.
I've run the program in simulation mode, and it works as expected.

That's interesting. I can only use NI19 to toggle the output; for example, with an output value of 25, turning it off and on with NI19 still keeps the output at 25. I want the output to start at zero again when I reactivate it with NI19.
Attached is a screen video showing an online test with a real [product_name] [version_no].

Thank you for your support. You are correct—the small section works standalone, but the full original program did not due to connection issues from pasting. Several connections were keeping the NI chain from resetting to zero. After some time troubleshooting, I resolved it, and everything works well now. It was a good learning experience.
Now you might see why it helps to upload the entire program rather than just a copied section.

analysis.insight_summary: The user struggled to reset analog output values using a digital input within a [product_name] sequence. The main issue stemmed from logic breaks created when program segments were copied, leading to confusion. After troubleshooting and peer feedback, the actual source was identified as broken connections in the copied code rather than device malfunction.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants a dependable method to reset the entire analog or mathematical sequence back to zero using a specific input, as consistently as in simpler program examples.
